text:
Jon R: hey team, customer reporting a spike of 429s during a short burst this morning. They say it looks like 'perceived throttling' even though quota shows available tokens.
Priya S: can you paste the exact error payload + client request ids? 429 Body and x-request-id help a lot.
Jon R: here — curl -> response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit"}}
```
Also sending our internal trace id: trace-9c7a
Sophia (support): thanks. Customer says they do continuous batching with small prompts (avg len ~30 tokens) but very high QPS spikes for 10-30s. They added KV prefix caching on those short sequences.
Eli M: interesting — with continuous batching you'll often see a backlog build in the batcher when a burst pushes concurrency. Even if overall token quota isn't exhausted, the realtime per-window throughput control can return 429s while background queues drain.
Jon R: they attached stack snippet showing they set batch_window_ms=20 and max_batch_size=64 and enabled kv_cache_prefix=true.
Priya S: small batch_window + kv cache + many small requests can create hot-path contention: KV cache lookups add a sync step before tokens are enqueued, increasing service time per request. That effectively reduces throughput headroom.
Jon R: customer asked if this is 'throttling' or a bug — they get 429s while metrics show quota left for the minute.
Eli M: it's expected behavior for enforced rate windows. Quota is usually evaluated at multiple levels: per-account token budget (minute/hour), and a short-term burst window (seconds) to protect latency SLOs. When batcher latency grows, short-window enforcement trips earlier.
Sophia (support): suggested repro steps to customer now — posting here in case infra wants to triage deeper.
infra-bot: alert: high-429s detected for acct: cust-445 on cluster cluster-3 at 2026-03-14T09:02:18Z (rate window triggers)
Priya S: repro steps (recommended):
1) Run a synthetic burst with similar payload distribution: 1000 requests over 15s with avg 30 tokens. Example using hey (or wrk):
```
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":40}' &
done
wait
```
2) Toggle kv cache off (kv_cache_prefix=false) and re-run the burst to compare 429 count and p95 latency.
3) If you can reproduce, collect diagnostics: the x-request-id list, the header x-batcher-latency-ms (if present), and a condensed CPU/mem snapshot of the serving node.
Jon R: customer ran step1 and saw 40% fewer 429s with kv cache disabled. Confirms contention.
Eli M: next steps from infra side: look at batcher metrics for that tenant during the burst window. Key metrics: queued_requests, batch_size_histogram, batch_latency_ms, kv_lookup_latency_ms. If kv_lookup_latency_ms spikes, that's the issue.
Priya S: mitigation options for customer:
- Increase allowed short-window QPS (requires plan change / support-assisted limit raise).
- Increase batch_window_ms slightly (let the batcher gather more before dispatch) — reduces per-request overhead.
- Turn off prefix KV caching for that specific route or set kv_cache_async=true if available.
- Add a client-side local debounce or leaky bucket to smooth arrival pattern.
Eli M: internal fix ideas:
- Add non-blocking KV cache path to let batcher enqueue while KV load is in-flight (async lookup then patch tokens).
- Improve observability: emit per-request kv cache latency and a cold/miss tag to correlate with 429 spikes.
Sophia (support): I've shared repro + suggested mitigations with the customer; they asked for a one-off short-window increase while they refactor. Can infra review the safety of a temporary bump?
Jon R: pinging infra for limit raise: trace ids attached.
Eli M: ok, I'll review cluster headroom and whether cluster-3 can absorb a short QPS bump for cust-445. If safe, support can enable a +2x short-window burst for 5 minutes while they migrate.
incidents-bot: note: change to rate limits must be recorded in audit logs. Requestor: Sophia. Ticket: INC-2026-334
Sophia (support): thanks — creating the change request now and emailing customer. Will post results here.
Jon R: one more thing — customer asked if changing model to a lower-latency variant reduces 429s. Answer: yes, smaller models finish faster and reduce batcher occupancy; adding lower-latency fallback works well for bursty workloads.
Priya S: closing loop: doc snippet to share with customer showing how to disable kv cache for route in their SDK config:
```json
{"route_config": {"kv_cache_prefix": false, "batch_window_ms": 40}}
```
Jon R: perfect — thanks team :thumbsup:
